brief: A two-storey storage tower for a workbench with at least two drawers.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;half-n on level 0 with piece:0,0,1;half-n stacked on level 1
drawer:0#0,0#cut and drawer:1#0,0#cut, one per storey

Drawers hold small parts (shown with M3 screws in the open lower drawer) and the top cover takes a roll of tape. Open edges are capped, the joints are bolted and there's a top cover. The configurator checks fit only, not strength or how much weight it can hold.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey storage tower with two drawers. Two north-half hex bases are stacked on cell (0,0), one on level 0 and one on level 1, and each has a drawer on its cut face. The open edges have solid end caps, the joints are bolted together and there's a cover on top. It comes to 23 parts, about 1229 g of filament and about 1770 minutes of printing. check_build reports no issues and the meshes are clear (no collisions). For display, the lower drawer is shown open with a small pile of M3 screws in it, and a roll of gaffer tape sits on the top cover. The screws sit below the drawer rim, so they're hard to see from the side. I also tried a pencil standing in the drawer, but it stood where the drawers open and would have stopped them, so I took it out.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
